title: ProviderShape
description: What a provider publishes about the shapes it may produce (spec.md §2). Not a contract: no consumer name, no evidence, no variants. Documents this schema treats as opaque are owned elsewhere: a shape is design 2.2's document.

$schema.description: Advisory: the schema this document claims to follow. Identifier only — a reader MUST NOT fetch it.

provenance.description: Document-level default provenance, in the RFC's decreasing order of fidelity (spec.md §2.3). Overridable per interaction. Never changes what the walk decides — it is policy input, not verdict input.

metadata.description: How the file came to exist. Open, following the same placement rule as contract spec §3.2.

writer.description: What produced this document: an open map of component name to version string.

interactions.description: One entry per operation the provider publishes a shape for. An interaction with no entry here gets no subsumption result at all (spec.md §2.2, §6.3) — not a passing one.

Party.title: Party
Party.description: A named party. Mirrors contract spec §3.1 so a broker already reading 'provider.name' keeps working.

StateRef.title: StateRef
StateRef.description: A provider state by name only — a provider shape does not know a given consumer's parameter values (spec.md §2.2).

ProviderInteraction.title: ProviderInteraction
ProviderInteraction.description: One operation's published shape. Matched to a consumer contract's interaction by 'description' plus 'states' names (spec.md §2.2, contract spec §4.2), or failing that by 'selector' (ADR 0025).

description.description: Matches a consumer interaction whose description is equal (spec.md §2.2); when no entry's does, 'selector' is tried instead.

states.description: Names only, no params (spec.md §2.2). On an entry matched by 'selector', present means the consumer's state names must also be equal; absent means the entry is about the operation in every state.

selector.description: Which consumer interactions this entry is about, for a provider that cannot know their descriptions (spec.md §2.2, ADR 0025): part name -> slot name -> shape, usually over request-direction slots (for HTTP, 'method' and 'path'). An entry selects an interaction when these shapes admit the values of every variant the contract recorded. Only ever matched against examples, never compared for subsumption.

provenance.description: Overrides the document-level 'provenance' for this interaction only.

source.description: Open provenance detail: a test-run reference for 'recorded', a type-schema location for 'derived', a verification-run window for 'observed'. Not interpreted by the walk.

parts.description: Part name -> slot name -> shape. Only the slots the provider produces belong here (spec.md §2.1) — this schema does not enforce that, since direction is the transport component's business, not the kernel's.

ShapePart.title: ShapePart
ShapePart.description: One part's shapes: slot name -> shape node. Each value is design 2.2's shape document, opaque here (contract spec §5.1's same nesting).
